subject.title: [Bug]: browser upload/file chooser flow is flaky and can misreport stale-click failures as browser control timeouts

question: Should Browser upload keep paths-only arm-then-later-click as a supported API, or should agent/tool flows move toward atomic upload-with-trigger behavior for dynamic pages?
rationale: Both paths are currently supported and documented as arming behavior; changing defaults could improve reliability while affecting callers that intentionally arm before a later trigger.

options.title: Compatibility-first atomic preference
options.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but make agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling prefer the existing same-request trigger path with tests and live proof.

options.title: Retire paths-only arming
options.body: Require a trigger ref/inputRef/element or direct input selector and provide migration guidance for delayed-trigger callers.

options.title: Document workaround only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document stale-ref recovery plus selector/batch mitigations while accepting the remaining flake.

recommendation.title: Compatibility-first atomic preference
recommendation.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but make agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling prefer the existing same-request trigger path with tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The live assignment plus Browser upload/client history make this the best available owner for the API contract choice.
